question.text: The alternative statute under which an AIF can be set up as an LLP pooling vehicle is:

explanation.text: The Logic: The Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 is the governing statute for LLP-form AIFs. The Partnership Act 1932 governs traditional partnerships (joint and several liability) which are NOT permitted as AIF vehicles. The Trap: The 1932 Act gives unlimited joint liability - not suitable as an AIF vehicle. 'LLP Rules 2013' is fabricated. Negotiable Instruments Act is irrelevant. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests this for all-cat managers. The exam distinguishes the 1932 Partnership Act (unlimited liability) from the 2008 LLP Act (limited liability). Manager's Pro-Tip: LLP structures in India are rare for AIFs because investor names become public on the MCA portal, compromising LP confidentiality. Trust structure is preferred for this very reason.
